lead: Tempe plumbing deals with very hard water, desert heat and 1960s and 1970s slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Tempe.
risk: very hard water scale, slab leaks and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and old pipes
why: North and central Tempe, including Maple-Ash and the area around ASU, have many homes from the 1950s to the 1970s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Many are rentals that see heavy use.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor are common. Very hard water scales up water heaters and fixtures.
water: Tempe treats Salt and Verde river water from SRP and Colorado River water from the Central Arizona Project. It is very hard.
tips: Flush your water heater every year.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Give tenants a shutoff valve map.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Tempe, Maple-Ash, the ASU area, Lakeshore, the Lakes, South Tempe, Warner Ranch and every other Tempe neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Tempe Community Development Department, and contractors need an Arizona Registrar of Contractors license.

faq.q: Do older Tempe homes need repiping?
faq.a: Many 1950s to 1970s homes still have galvanized steel supply pipes. They rust inside, which lowers pressure and causes leaks. PEX or copper repiping fixes both.
